Title:
Untying Prefill and Decode Loops in Looped Language Models

Authors:
Yang Hu

Primary category: cs.CL (Computation and Language)
Cross-list: cs.LG (Machine Learning)

Comments:
27 pages, 13 figures. Code, per-item results and a script that recomputes every number: https://github.com/yanghu819/untying-prefill-decode

License: CC BY 4.0

Abstract (plain text):
Looped language models run a block of layers several times per token and use the same number of loops to read the prompt (prefill) and to generate each token (decode). Generation, however, is almost all decoding. On Ouro-2.6B at batch 1, prefill takes 0.4-2.8% of the time of a chain-of-thought answer, so extra prefill loops cost little. We untie the two loop counts and read the prompt with more loops than we use to decode each token. The released model cannot use the states of a longer prefill, so we distill a small adapter (2.4% of the parameters): LoRA on the decoder for a fixed prefill depth, or LoopBridge, whose per-loop key and value maps keep long-context accuracy when one adapter serves every trained pair of depths. On Ouro-2.6B with one decode loop, four prefill loops raise the average over 11 benchmarks from 44.2 to 57.1 (56.8 with LoopBridge), above the original model distilled to one loop on the same data (49.8), and in the same measured time per request they are 14-15 points more accurate than the original model. The gain peaks after two to five prefill loops and holds on Ouro-1.4B, the Thinking models and looped decision models. Code: https://github.com/yanghu819/untying-prefill-decode
